skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with bilateral patchy opacities to distinguish organizing pneumonia from other interstitial or nodular lung diseases.
steps: Check for the presence of bilateral, patchy consolidations or opacities that are predominantly distributed in the peripheral (subpleural) regions of the lungs.

Distinguish this pattern from sarcoidosis by confirming the absence of perilymphatic nodules (typically upper/mid-zone predominant) and from Wegener's granulomatosis by confirming the absence of cavitary lesions or distinct nodules.
